title: Dispatch: bootstrap capability ledger and eshyra-2n1t reconciliation (attempt 1)
description:
SUPERVISOR PRE-PLANNING. Implement exactly what is specified here. Read the
parent spec first: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1`.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.md
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/2n1t-engine-closure-reconciliation.md
  packages/core/src/rules/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts
Do NOT edit package.json, packages/core/package.json, or
packages/core/src/internal.ts. npm-script wiring is deferred. Your test imports
the module by relative path ('../src/rules/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.js').

=== THE CENTRAL CONSTRAINT — DO NOT DERIVE THIS FROM THE PACK ALONE ===
The current pack OMITS whole clauses. A ledger generated only from its projected
mechanics inherits exactly the blind spots this audit exposed. If legendary-
action budgets are absent from the pack, deriving requirements from the pack
cannot discover that a legendary-budget capability is needed. Assemble from FIVE
sources:

  1. Current readiness artifacts: `record.data.executionReadiness` in
     packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, plus the
     2026-07-06 inventories already in docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/
     (execution-boundary-classification, engine-coverage-inventory,
     rule-classification, magic-item-mechanics-inventory, and siblings).
  2. Current code: what @eshyra/core actually implements today. Read it.
  3. Current open AND CLOSED beads (`bd list --status=closed` matters here as
     much as open ones).
  4. Every accepted audit finding from the 2026-07-24 reviews. Read
     /mnt/d/eshyra-2026-07-24-audit-repair-bead-plan.md in full.
  5. Source clauses KNOWN to be missing from current projection, taken from the
     findings themselves: legendary-action budgets, point-origin geometry,
     multi-save entries, rider damage, half-damage branches, pit variants, and
     the rest named in the plan.

PROOF OBLIGATION: the ledger must demonstrably contain at least one capability
that the pack's current projected mechanics could NOT have revealed (the
legendary-action budget is the canonical example). Mark such rows with their
discovering source. A test must assert that at least one row's only discovering
sources are non-pack sources. That assertion is the evidence the five-source
method actually worked; without it this bead has not been done.

=== LEDGER ROW SHAPE ===
  capabilityId         qualified, e.g. engine:F5
  requirement          the specific primitive, not the family label
  discoveredBy[]       which of the five sources revealed it
  packEvidence         clause/record keys or a generated query — never a count
  codeEvidence         what exists today in @eshyra/core, if anything
  owningBead           an EXISTING bead ID (see below)
  ownershipStatus      owned | proposed-new-bead | disputed
  notes

OWNERSHIP: the ten engine:F* family epics under eshyra-olc5 already exist and
are the legitimate owners for capabilities that fit a family. Implementation
children deliberately DO NOT exist yet — they are created later by the
per-family decomposition tasks, so do not invent them. Where a requirement fits
no existing bead, set ownershipStatus=proposed-new-bead and record the proposed
title and parent as DATA. Do NOT create, reopen, or close any bead yourself.

=== REQUIRED DELIVERABLE: the eshyra-2n1t contradiction ===
eshyra-2n1t (the "engine F1-F10" epic) was CLOSED 2026-07-21 claiming full
worktree / test / importer-reproducibility / freeze verification. Three days
later the audit found 794 engine-pending magic-item clauses in the committed
pack. Produce 2n1t-engine-closure-reconciliation.md classifying EACH old bead
into exactly one of:

  * DIFFERENT SCOPE OR TAXONOMY — correctly closed; never claimed the newly
    identified capability. Most likely for the beads loosely matching
    engine:F1/F4/F8/F9/F10, given the taxonomy divergence.
  * STALE READINESS MAPPING — the code exists, but readiness artifacts failed to
    recognize it.
  * INCOMPLETE INTEGRATION — a primitive exists but is not wired into the
    required execution path.
  * PREMATURE CLOSURE — the stated acceptance was objectively not satisfied.

Beads to reconcile, ALL currently closed: eshyra-2n1t and its children,
eshyra-2n1t.1, eshyra-2n1t.2, eshyra-b69j.13, eshyra-o9bd.18.7,
eshyra-o9bd.18.7.8.

PRESERVE HISTORICAL TRUTH. Do not auto-reopen anything and do not modify these
beads. Where you conclude a child should be reopened or a corrective child
created, record that as a RECOMMENDATION in the document with its evidence; the
supervisor executes it. eshyra-2n1t already carries a note pointing at this
reconciliation — do not add another.

Note the taxonomy trap: eshyra-2n1t's F1-F10 are NOT the pack's engine:F1-F10.
That epic used F1 dice-grammar, F4 spell-slot economy, F8 character-build gap
closures, F9 derived-math primitives, F10 currency surface. A same-numbered
child there does NOT cover the same-numbered pack capability family. Your
classification must be argued per bead, not per number.

=== bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts + test ===
  * load and schema-validate the ledger JSON;
  * verify every owningBead reference is well-formed, and check existence via
    `bd` when available — SKIP gracefully when the `bd` binary is absent, in
    the style of the repo's dolt-gated tests;
  * verify no row stores a count where a query belongs;
  * verify every capabilityId uses the qualified engine:F* form;
  * assert the non-pack-discovery proof obligation above;
  * assert every one of engine:F1..engine:F10 appears at least once.

The ledger must be labelled NON-AUTHORITATIVE in both the JSON and the .md. The
authoritative ledger is eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12 and is generated later from the
clause-complete corpus; this one is a bootstrap and will be diffed against it.

Pack shape notes: records use the `key` field, NOT `id` — searching by id
silently returns nothing. executionReadiness lives at
`record.data.executionReadiness`, not `record.executionReadiness`.

=== NAMING HAZARD — READ BEFORE WRITING ANY IDENTIFIER ===
"F1".."F10" means THREE different things in this repository:
  engine:F1..F10    pack executionReadiness engineHooks[].engine families
  fable:F1..F8      Fable 5 audit findings
  opus:F-01..F-35   Opus 5 audit findings
  sol:CAP-001..014  GPT-5.6-Sol agent audit findings
  indep:001..012    independent review findings (renamed from SOL-*)
Never write a bare "F5" or a bare "CAP-002". Always qualify with the prefix.
The CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t used yet another F1-F10 taxonomy that does NOT
correspond to engine:F1-F10 except loosely at F2/F3/F5/F7.

=== COUNT HYGIENE ===
No test and no committed artifact may depend on a hand-copied number (391, 399,
77, 79, 794, 1016, 1813). Every count is a SNAPSHOT of commit 4384f25. Where a
count matters, commit the QUERY that generates it and let the number be derived
at run time.

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
Run `npm ci` in this worktree FIRST. Worktrees have no node_modules of their
own and will otherwise resolve @eshyra/core through the parent checkout's stale
dist/*.d.ts and report phantom typecheck errors.
Then run `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it rewrites files
(Biome formats and organizes imports), so verifying after committing means the
committed tree is not the tree that passed.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
* Edit ONLY the files listed under "FILES YOU OWN". Two sibling dispatches are
  running in parallel right now on disjoint file sets. Touching anything else —
  especially package.json, packages/core/package.json, or
  packages/core/src/internal.ts — will collide with them. If you believe you
  need a file outside your list, record that in your completion notes instead
  and stop short of editing it.
* Do NOT modify any bead except your own. Do NOT run `bd dolt push`. If you
  discover follow-up work, use `bd create` and say so in your notes.
* Do NOT push, do NOT open or comment on a pull request, do NOT merge.
  AGENTS.md's standing push authority does not apply to you on this dispatch;
  integration belongs to the agent that dispatched you. Committed work on your
  branch is a complete handoff.
* Do NOT weaken, skip, or delete any existing test or audit expectation.
* Do NOT regenerate the rules pack and do NOT run the SRD importer.
acceptance_criteria:
• Ledger assembled from all five sources and explicitly labelled non-authoritative.
• At least one row is discoverable only from non-pack sources, and a test asserts it.
• Every engine:F1..F10 family appears; every capabilityId is qualified.
• Every row maps to an existing bead or carries ownershipStatus=proposed-new-bead with a proposed title and parent.
• 2n1t reconciliation classifies every listed bead into exactly one of the four categories, with per-bead argument rather than per-number.
• No bead is created, reopened, or closed by this dispatch.
• npm run verify:worktree passes from this worktree.
• No file outside the owned list is modified.
